items.why: The report only implies this through SNR, noting that "Signal-to-noise differs by roughly an order of magnitude between temperatures" (4K 587.7 nm 1106.9 vs 295K 54.6). It treats this as a data-quality issue and never states that the A1' Raman intensity rises on cooling.
The report never says the resonance maximum shifts with temperature or follows the exciton energy. It states "the A-exciton energy at 4, 150 and 295 K" was "not verified".
The report does not describe exciton/trion or incoming/outgoing structure at low temperature versus a single broad peak at room temperature.
The report does not discuss trion versus exciton contributions or their temperature dependence.

The report warns that "Intensity trends at fixed nominal wavelength mix temperature and resonance". However, it attributes this mainly to laser energies not matching across temperatures, and it does not say that a full excitation profile is needed at each temperature.
The report never mentions thin-film interference on 290 nm SiO2/Si or its temperature dependence.
The report asks "how was the sample temperature measured? Laser heating at 0.7 mW on a supported flake can shift the local temperature by an unknown amount."

wrong_claims.why: The report does not attribute any intensity change to the Bose-Einstein factor.
The report makes no claim about which direction the resonance shifts.
